title: Appelsin-Limonade (Orange Lemonade)
description: Prepared with orange, oranges, and cochineal.
steps: Peel oranges very thinly and place the peel in a bottle in which you pour so much spirits that it stands somewhat over the peel
Let it stand corked for 3 months to infuse
When you want to make the lemonade, dissolve 1½ pounds fine sugar in 2 pots boiling water with 4 quintals citric acid
When it is dissolved and cooled, add 2 drams of the orange essence with 14 quintals cochineal drops
This lemonade is especially suitable for children

title: Appelsin-Marmelade (Orange Jam)
description: A fruit preserve made with oranges, lemon, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: At least 1/4 kg powdered sugar per 1/2 kg fruit meat
ingredients.sourceText: At least 1/4 kg powdered sugar per 1/2 kg fruit meat

ingredients.name: the last cooking water in which the fruit was boiled
ingredients.sourceText: 1/4 liter of the last cooking water in which the fruit was boiled

steps: Cook the fruit in water until completely soft so it can easily be pierced with a straw or stick
Change the water 2 to 3 times during cooking, which lasts about one hour
Dry the fruit and cut the yellow peel as thin as possible, then cut into thread-fine strips
Remove the bitter white pith and cut the fruit open, carefully removing the seeds
Weigh the fruit meat with the juice
Cook sugar and water for 10 minutes, then add the orange mixture and cook for another 10 minutes
Finally add the finely cut peel and cook the jam for 10 minutes more until ready to pour into glasses and seal
The best time for making this jam is February, March, or April when fresh bitter oranges are available

title: Appelsingelée (Orange Jelly)
description: Prepared with oranges, white sugar, and juice.
steps: Rub the zest of 5 oranges on ½ pound white sugar.
Strain the juice of 5 oranges and 2 lemons and pour into a saucepan with 2 pints water, 2 pints white wine, 12 quarters dissolved isinglass, and 3 to 4 beaten egg whites.
Set over a brisk heat and bring to a boil, lift off for a moment, bring to a boil again, and repeat this a third time, and after skimming it should appear clear.
Pour it through a filter bag to clarify and fill what drains into clear glass bowls, which are set on ice or in a cold place.

title: Appelsintærte (Orange Tart)
description: A pastry dish made with orange, egg yolks, and icing sugar.

ingredients.name: Egg whites, whipped to stiff peaks
ingredients.sourceText: Egg whites, whipped to stiff peaks

ingredients.name: Orange or lemon cream (prepared as Nr. 273)
ingredients.sourceText: Orange or lemon cream (prepared as Nr. 273)

ingredients.name: White sugar glaze with orange juice
ingredients.sourceText: White sugar glaze with orange juice

steps: Whisk the egg yolks with {{source-1}}.
Melt half a pound butter in a warm oven and sift {{source-3}} on white paper.
When the sugar and eggs are whisked completely white, add the warm butter, then the flour, and finally the whipped egg whites and the grated zest of 5 lemons.
Cut paper to fit the pan size as molds, crimp the edges and brush with cold butter.
Distribute the mixture into these molds and bake until light brown.
Between the layers from the molds, place the orange or lemon cream.
Carefully trim the edges and cover the entire tart with a glaze of white sugar dissolved in water and mixed with a little orange juice.
Place in the oven to dry.

Dry orange slices (with seeds removed) in a lukewarm oven, glaze them by dipping with a thin pointed stick into boiled white sugar, and when dry, arrange in a ring on the outer edge of the cake's top layer.
Decorate the whole cake with decorative sugar glaze in figures, in whose larger spaces you can place jelly.

title: Apple Butter
description: Prepared with cider and apples.

ingredients.name: All sorts of apples, if only they are juicy
ingredients.sourceText: All sorts of apples, if only they are juicy

steps: Fill a kettle with cider and let it boil until about one-third is boiled away.
Peel the apples, cut them into small pieces, free them from the cores and put so many in the kettle that the cider covers them.
Let it boil evenly with frequent stirring. When the apples are fully soft, take them up with a fish slice so that no juice comes with.
Put a new batch of chopped apples in the cider in the same way as before, and treat them in the same manner.
Then remove the kettle from the fire and pour everything into a spacious crock, where it stands until the next day under a well-fitting lid.
Then pour it back into the kettle and cook again with constant stirring until it is brown and like soft soap. Can be seasoned with cinnamon and cloves to taste.
Pour into stone crocks and will, in a dry, cool place, keep through the winter.

title: Apricots (Abrikoser)
description: Prepared with apricots, powdered sugar, and juice.

ingredients.name: 3/4 pot cold water per pound of fruit
ingredients.sourceText: 3/4 pot cold water per pound of fruit

ingredients.name: as many pounds of powdered sugar as the fruit weighs
ingredients.sourceText: as many pounds of powdered sugar as the fruit weighs

ingredients.name: as many measures of water as sugar
ingredients.sourceText: as many measures of water as sugar

steps: The fruit must be barely ripe and dried before placing in a preserving kettle with 3/4 pot cold water per pound.
When the apricots are tender, remove them and lay on clean linen to dry.
Cut them in half, remove the stones, and peel the skin if desired.
Cook equal parts powdered sugar and water with the sugar measure of water into a syrup, skim well, and add the juice of one lemon.
Cook the fruit in the syrup until clear, then remove and place in a preserving jar.
Pour the syrup over them and add a little brandy or spirits on top.
Note: Apricots and peaches tend to ferment quickly and require frequent monitoring, and if necessary must be cooked again with more sugar.

title: Artis-Suppe (Root Vegetable Soup)
description: A soup made with carrots, celery, and leeks.
steps: Cut all the vegetables into pieces, approximately one inch long and of the thickness of a finger.
After the vegetables are washed, drain the water from them on a colander.
Put 2 ounces of butter on the fire; when it is melted, add the vegetables and cook for a quarter hour with constant stirring, so that it does not brown.
Then add salt, a few whole peppercorns and 2.5 quarts of water, but only 0.5 quart at a time, and in such a way that it boils between each addition.
In total the soup must cook for about two hours, and to prevent it from boiling over, it must simmer evenly and with a lid on.
If you find that there are too many vegetables, some of them can be held back during serving.
It is served with toasted bread and is for 3 to 4 persons.

title: Asier (Pickled Cucumbers)
description: Prepared with cucumbers, vinegar, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: (10 quintals) whole yellow mustard seeds
ingredients.sourceText: 50 grams (10 quintals) whole yellow mustard seeds

ingredients.name: A couple dozen small peeled shallots
ingredients.sourceText: A couple dozen small peeled shallots

steps: Choose short, thick, heavy green cucumbers for pickling
Peel them, split lengthwise, and scrape out the seeds with a silver spoon
Sprinkle with salt and set aside until the next day
Remove from the brine, drain well, and dry in cloth
Heat the vinegar with the powdered sugar, long pepper, whole white pepper, whole yellow mustard seeds (wrapped in a clear piece of cloth), Spanish pepper pods, dill, and peeled shallots
Boil all of this in the vinegar, then remove after 2 minutes before the cucumbers are added
Arrange the cucumbers in a crock and after all are arranged, bring the vinegar to a boil before pouring it over the cucumbers
Place the mustard seeds on top of the crock, cover with cloth, and the next day bind with parchment paper
Cucumbers pickled this way become hard, crisp, and very durable

title: Asier med Ingefær (Pears with Ginger)
description: Prepared with ginger, pears, and vinegar.
steps: Peel the pears, split them, hollow them out with a silver spoon and dry them in a cloth, before cutting them across into narrow strips, either with an ordinary knife or with an herb knife.
Soak the ginger in water until the next day; then scald, scrape, rinse and cook it together with the vinegar and sugar to a thin syrup, into which the pear pieces are placed.
Cook for about 5 minutes and drain on a sieve, and the syrup is cooked until smooth, together with the ginger.
The pears are put back into the pot to blend with the syrup, before they are filled into the jar, which is sealed when the preserve has cooled.
The ginger may remain in the jar among the pears, or it may be removed and wrapped in a clear cloth to be placed on top of the jar.

title: Asier med Kirsebærsaft (Pickled Cucumbers with Cherry Juice)
description: Prepared with cucumbers, cherry, and vinegar.
steps: Peel the cucumbers, hollow them, weigh them and put them on the stove with enough vinegar to cook them in
When they have had one boil, remove them, press in cloths and cut into strips
If they are small cucumbers, you do not need to cut them into strips
For 1/2 pound of cucumbers, take 1 gill raw cherry juice, 2 small spoonfuls of vinegar, 1/2 pound sugar, 5 cloves and some small pieces of cinnamon
Put this on the stove and boil until it just simmers
Add the cucumbers, and when it boils again, remove them and place in the crock
Boil the liquid for a few more minutes and pour it hot over
Cover with a cloth and tie up the next day

title: Asparges, som Slikasparges (Asparagus as Sauce Asparagus)
description: A sauce made with asparagus, salt, and butter.
steps: Rinse the asparagus in cold water
Peel from top to bottom to remove the woody outer part at the lower end
Trim the bottom
Tie them in bundles of about twenty pieces
Cook in water with a little salt for about a quarter hour until tender, but not so tender that the heads fall off
Remove the ties from the bundles and arrange on a flat platter with a napkin underneath
If they are barely tender enough, cover them with a warm napkin and let them stand for a moment until done
For sauce asparagus, always choose the largest and most tender with light heads

title: Asparges-Budding (Asparagus Pudding)
description: A pudding made with asparagus, powdered sugar, and egg yolks.
steps: Bake together the flour, butter, powdered sugar and sweet milk.
Stir in 12 egg yolks, two at a time, a little ground nutmeg, and finally the beaten egg whites.
Cook 15 large asparagus until tender in salted water and place on a colander to drain.
Cut each asparagus into 3-5 pieces.
Layer the asparagus pieces with the batter in a buttered and breadcrumb-lined pudding mold.
Cook the pudding for 2 hours and serve warm with melted butter.

title: Asparges-Omelet (Asparagus Omelet)
description: Prepared with asparagus, cream, and egg yolks.
steps: Peel good asparagus, cut into thumb-length pieces and cook in water until tender
Make a sauce of 12 drams butter and 15 drams flour, thin with 1 measure cream
Add the cooked asparagus with salt, sugar and a little nutmeg
Stir well together with 6 egg yolks
Carefully fold in the beaten egg whites
Pour the entire mixture into a buttered and breadcrumbed dish
Bake for half an hour in a warm oven

description: A salad made with asparagus, vinegar, and water.
steps: Peel and cut asparagus small and cook tender in a small amount of water.

title: Asparges-Suppe (Asparagus Soup)
description: A soup made with asparagus, veal or lamb or stock, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: (5 pots) veal or lamb stock, or economical stock
ingredients.sourceText: 5 L (5 pots) veal or lamb stock, or economical stock

steps: Brown the butter with the flour and dilute with the stock in which a bunch of herbs has been cooked
Peel the asparagus and cut into pieces 3 centimeters (about 1 inch) in length and cook for a quarter hour in the stock
Add the asparagus heads a few minutes later, as they require less cooking than the rest of the asparagus
Whisk the egg yolks with a spoonful of cold water and then blend with some of the hot stock before stirring it into the pot with constant stirring
Do not allow the soup to boil while the eggs are being stirred in, nor afterwards, as it will curdle
If using canned asparagus, use 1 kilo (2.5 lb) tin, blend the water with the stock, and add the asparagus to the pot just before serving
Serve with toasted or baked bread

In a tureen, beat 6 egg yolks with 6 tablespoons of good sweet cream.
Under continuous beating, carefully add the soup a little at a time to the egg mixture.
Serve with toasted French bread cut into cubes.

title: At koge Kjød frisk igen (Cooking Meat Fresh Again)
description: Prepared with meat.
steps: In warm weather, if meat and flesh develop what is called a 'taint' in kitchen language, place it on the fire in a little water along with some charcoal.
Boil for a quarter hour with the charcoal, which will restore the meat to freshness.
To prevent the charcoal from leaving marks on the meat, wrap it in a very thin piece of cloth.

title: At koge sur Suppesaft igen (Cooking Sour Stock Again)
description: Prepared with meat stock and meat or bones.

ingredients.name: raw or cooked, chopped meat bones (fresh and good)
ingredients.sourceText: raw or cooked, chopped meat bones (fresh and good)

steps: If preserved meat stock from one day to the next becomes sour in summer, boil the soup for a quarter hour or longer if needed with some raw or cooked, chopped meat bones.
The sourness will be boiled away by the chalky substance contained in the bones, and the soup will become good and usable.
Alternatively, let the sour food boil quite dry with a teaspoon of magnesia, which will remove all sourness.

title: At koge ved Damp (Cooking by Steam)
description: Prepared with vegetables or meat or fish, water, and salt.

ingredients.name: vegetables, meat, fish, or poultry to be cooked
ingredients.sourceText: vegetables, meat, fish, or poultry to be cooked

steps: Obtain a simple, deep tin pot with a lid that fits tightly and well.
Place a tin sieve inside that goes only one quarter of the way down into the pot (it must not have a handle or shaft).
Fill one quarter of the space below with water.
Place the sieve in, add what is to be cooked, sprinkle with salt, place the lid on, and keep the water in continuous boil until the vegetables are tender.
The water becomes a strong stock that can be used in many ways.

title: At koge Æggekelvide (Cooking Egg Whites)
description: Prepared with egg whites and milk.
steps: Place milk on the fire in a shallow pan; when it boils, add the egg whites, which have been beaten to stiff foam, one spoonful beside the other.
They need only boil a moment to become large, then remove them and place them on an inverted sieve so the milk can drain off.
Sugar, a piece of vanilla or cinnamon can be added to the milk, which gives the whites a good taste.
The milk can then be strained off and used for egg milk and the like.

title: At lave Glasér-Sukker (Making Icing Sugar)
description: Prepared with egg white, white sugar, and juice or lemon.

ingredients.name: white sugar (finely ground and sifted)
ingredients.sourceText: 3 ounces white sugar (finely ground and sifted)

ingredients.name: juice of one lemon or half a lemon
ingredients.sourceText: juice of one lemon or half a lemon

steps: Beat the egg white to foam and stir it well with 3 ounces of very good, finely ground and sifted white sugar.
If it does not become as thick as a thin porridge, more sugar should be added, as otherwise it will not be able to cover the cake.
Stir in the juice of a lemon or half a lemon and a little rose water.
To make the cake, which is to be iced, even, rub it with flour before coating it with the icing.

title: At nedlægge Spegesild (Preserved Spiced Herring)
description: Prepared with fat and salt.
steps: Clean the herring by removing the gills
Sprinkle generously with salt and let stand for 3 days
Remove the herring and brush off the salt
Layer the herring in a small barrel or half-barrel with the belly side up, packed tightly together
Between each layer of herring, place a good layer of salt, and top with salt
Once layered, place a weight on top

title: At udtage Skroget og farsere en Kalkun (Boning and Stuffing a Turkey)
description: Prepared with turkey and salt.
steps: Place the plucked, cleaned and washed turkey on a cloth with the breast facing down toward the table.
With a pointed, sharp knife, slit the skin along the back.
With great care, cut out the back and breast bone in such a way that only the thighs and wings remain attached to the meat, but this must be done without damaging the skin.
When the turkey is opened in this manner, remove the entrails at the same time as the skeleton.
Spread the meat out on the cloth, sprinkle with a little salt and cover with enough stuffing that the turkey, when sewn together along the back, has taken on a beautiful round shape.

title: Aubain (Aubain Meatloaf)
description: Prepared with egg yolks, onion, and meat.
steps: Melt the butter and bake the flour in it.
Add the boiling milk gradually to the flour mixture.
When cooled, stir in the egg yolks, grated onion, salt, pepper and chopped meat.
Finally fold in the beaten egg whites.
Pour into a buttered and floured pudding mold.
Boil for 2.5 hours.
Alternatively, bake in the oven in a gratin dish for approximately 1 hour or in a ring mold.
Serve with a brown gravy sauce made with gherkins, anchovies, pickles, pearl onions, chutney, Maggi bouillon cubes or lemon juice.

title: Aubin (Meat and Cream Pudding)
description: A pudding made with meat, onions, and egg yolks.
steps: Chop the cooked meat very finely with some onions.
Bake it with {{source-2}}, {{source-3}} and 3 pints cooked milk.
When baked, pour it into a dish, and when it has cooled, stir 15 egg yolks into it.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks and fold in last.
Put the mixture in a pudding mold greased with butter and sprinkled with breadcrumbs and cook for 1.5 hours.
Serve with a strong sauce of meat broth, to which a very little Sherry can be added.

title: Bagte Snegle i Brøddejg (Baked Snails in Bread Dough)
description: A bread preparation made with bread, snails, and mushrooms.
steps: Finely chop 125 grams mushrooms together with 1 onion
Sauté in {{source-2}}
Add as much grated French bread as the butter can accommodate
Thin with the strongly reduced, strained snail broth until it reaches the consistency of a not too thin batter dough
Season with salt, pepper and a little white wine or lemon juice
Stir in {{source-8}}
Ensure snail shells are well cleaned inside with boiling and cold water and well drained
Place a little of the dough in each shell
Add the cooked snail (from No. 572)
Cover with dough and smooth it
Sprinkle with finely sifted breadcrumbs
Drizzle with melted butter
Place in a moderately warm oven
Bake for about 15 minutes on a baking pan covered with a layer of kitchen salt, or on a flat dish
Arrange very hot on a napkin, decorated with salad and garnished with lemon, whose juice is eaten on the snails

title: Bankekød (Braised Beef)
description: Prepared with beef or chuck, butter or lard, and onion.

ingredients.name: beef chuck or mixed cut
ingredients.sourceText: 3 kg beef chuck or mixed cut

steps: Cut the meat into slices, which are beaten out with a meat mallet and dipped in a mixture of salt, pepper, and flour.
In a pot, brown a good slice of butter, lard, or Palmin, and in it brown a dessert plate of finely chopped onion, after which the floured meat is placed in the pot.
Pour over it 1 liter water or thin stock and coloring, sufficient to color the sauce.
Simmer the meat over low heat and under a closed lid for about 3 hours.
Add Maggi bouillon cubes in this and the following 2 dishes if the sauce is not sufficiently piquant.
Serve with boiled potatoes or mashed potatoes.
When the meat is about tender, raw, peeled, cut potatoes can be added to cook in the sauce.

title: Bavarol (Bavarian Cream)
description: Prepared with cream, isinglass, and powdered sugar.
steps: Dissolve isinglass in boiling water along with powdered sugar and pour into cold rhubarb juice.
When it begins to set, stir in whipped cream made from the heavy cream.
Pour it into a wetted and sprinkled mold.
Place in a cool location or on ice for a few hours.
Serve with small macaroons.
Either red currant, raspberry, strawberry, or cherry juice can be used instead of rhubarb.
If the juice is sweet, use less sugar.
Can be decorated with preserved fruits around the pudding.

description: Prepared with beef, wheat flour, and onion.
steps: Use Porterhouse or sirloin. Have the butcher cut it into thick or thin slices as you prefer.
Pound thick slices lightly on both sides, then sprinkle with salt and pepper and fry in brown butter.
When done, which varies according to taste, place on a platter.
Put a piece of butter on the pan, stir in 1 teaspoon wheat flour, some grated onion and a little ground pepper, then thin with boiling water.

If you have bouillon, make a better sauce as follows: When the meat is taken from the pan, add butter and stir well with a spoon; when it is brown, add grated onion and cook a little. Then stir in good bouillon and ground pepper.

title: Beefsteg på Rist (Grilled Beef Steak)
description: Prepared with beef, butter, and salt.
steps: Use Porterhouse beef for steak. Skin it and scrape it from the sides; make cuts here and there in the meat so that it cooks through more easily.
Place it on the grill and cook over clear coals of hardwood. When you think it is cooked enough on one side, turn it.
Do not let it become too dry; it should be red inside.
When done, place it on a platter, lay cold butter and salt over it and let it rest a moment in the oven, but serve it before the butter is completely melted. Eat it with potatoes.

title: Benlose Fugle (Boneless Birds)
description: Prepared with beef, carrot or meat, and onion.
steps: Thin slices of beef are cut and beaten very little.
On each piece is spread a spoonful of beef forcemeat, into which is placed a narrow piece of carrot or fatty meat, which is first dipped in spices.
The meat is folded together and formed in the shape of a bird without head and legs.
The meat is packed together with meat and bound with twine.
The birds are rubbed with flour, pepper, a little crushed cloves and salt.
A piece of butter is browned, in which a grated onion is boiled, then the birds, until they are slightly brown.

This is thinned with water and broth until it stands over them, and boiled gently for a couple of hours or until they are tender, then they are placed on a platter and kept warm, while the sauce is strained, put back on the fire with a little cream and flour if it is not strong and even enough, and poured over the birds.
These can be made in the same way without forcemeat, only with a piece of carrot or meat in the middle.

title: Biscuits Nr. 1
description: A biscuit made with fat, flour, and baking powder.
steps: Sift {{source-0}} with {{source-1}} and {{source-2}}.
Rub {{source-3}} quickly into the flour in small pieces.
Dust the dough pan and table with flour.
Pour 1 quart cold milk into the dough and blend as quickly as possible.
Turn the dough onto the table, roll out 1 inch thick, and cut the small biscuits into squares and place on a buttered baking pan.

Bake in a hot oven. All of this must be done with the greatest haste so the biscuits can get into the oven before the gas from the baking powder and milk escapes. The dough is made light by this gas, which forces itself up through it, but if the biscuits are not baked before the gas escapes, they will be heavy.
When half-baked—after about 10 minutes—open the oven door and brush a little milk over them, then finish baking.

title: Blaabær-, Hyldebær- og Solbærsuppe (Blueberry, Elderberry, and Blackcurrant Soup)
description: A soup made with blueberries or elderberries or blackcurrants, potato flour, and lemon juice or fruit juice.

ingredients.name: 3 pots blueberries, or 14 pounds ripe elderberries, or 12 pots blackcurrants
ingredients.sourceText: 3 pots blueberries, or 14 pounds ripe elderberries, or 12 pots blackcurrants

ingredients.name: lemon juice or sour fruit juice
ingredients.sourceText: lemon juice or sour fruit juice

ingredients.name: bread balls or baked wheat bread cubes
ingredients.sourceText: bread balls or baked wheat bread cubes

steps: Clean the berries well and put them on to cook with the water until they are so tender that they can be mashed through a sieve. The cooking will take about an hour.
Strain the soup and put it back over the fire with a couple of sticks of cinnamon and a little lemon peel and cook it, then skim it.
Mix 2 to 3 teaspoonfuls of potato flour in a little cold water and thin it with a little of the soup.
Add sugar to taste, add the thickening to the soup, give it just one boil, but no more.
If the soup needs more sourness, add a little lemon juice or sour fruit juice.
Serve it with bread balls on top or with baked wheat bread cubes on the side.
Elderberry soup gets a good flavor when you take pieces of peeled good apples, with the cores removed, and cook them in the soup after it has been strained.

title: Blaabærsaft (Blueberry Juice)
description: Prepared with blueberries.

ingredients.name: (1 Pot) water per 2 to 2½ kg berries (optional)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 liter (1 Pot) water per 2 to 2½ kg berries (optional)

steps: Boil the berries for a quarter of an hour with frequent stirring.
Press the juice through a very fine sieve.
Pour it into bottles, which are wrapped with hay, corked, and boiled for 5 minutes in the pot.
When the bottles have partially cooled, wipe them dry and plaster them the next day.
Alternatively, the blueberries can be boiled with 1 liter (1 Pot) water per 2 to 2½ kg berries.
Sift off the juice and treat as described above.

title: Black Cherries, Preserving Cherries (Sorte Kirsebær)
description: Prepared with cherries, vinegar, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar equal in weight to the berries
ingredients.sourceText: powdered sugar equal in weight to the berries

steps: Remove the stones from large, ripe berries and place them in a terrine, covering with enough good vinegar to cover the berries.
Let sit overnight.
The next day, pour the berries into a colander so all vinegar drains off.
Weigh the berries and for each pound take 1 pound powdered sugar.
On the bottom of a preserving jar place, for the stated quantity, 4 drams whole cinnamon and 15 drams whole cloves.
Over this lay a 3-fingers-thick layer of powdered sugar, then a layer of cherries, then a layer of sugar, continuing in this manner with the top layer being a 4-fingers-thick sugar layer.
Tie the jar immediately with a bladder and place in a cool location.
The drained vinegar can be bottled and used in other ways, such as for sweet soup and similar.

title: Blanc Manger (Almond Jelly)
description: Prepared with cream, sweet almonds, and bitter almonds.

ingredients.name: 2 Ounces isinglass, dissolved in warm water
ingredients.sourceText: 2 Ounces isinglass, dissolved in warm water

steps: Heat the sweet cream with the whole sugar, finely pounded sweet almonds, finely pounded bitter almonds, and lemon zest
When it has boiled for 2 to 3 minutes, add the isinglass dissolved in warm water
Cook gently for 10 minutes with constant stirring
Strain through a fine cloth into a stone bowl
For the red jelly layer: mix together the raspberry juice, cherry juice, water, white sugar, and gelatine
Bring to a boil, stirring, and stir in a bowl until it begins to set
When both parts are ready, pour some of the white mixture into the oiled mold to a height of about half an inch
Insert a clean stick and make a cut where the mixture ends
When completely cold and stiff, warm some of the red jelly so it is just fluid and carefully pour it over with a spoon so it does not fall hard on one spot and break the white
Hold the stick, which must not be pointed, down to the solid layer and pour, filling to the cut
Continue in this way as long as there is something left
Keep the mold in cold water the entire time, changing it often
This pudding is always turned out
Always test each mixture before putting it in the mold by pouring a little onto a saucer and letting it cool and set as much as possible
The white never fails, but the red depends much on the quality of the juice; homemade juice should be used; if it does not set, use more gelatine

title: Blanc-manger (Blancmange)
description: Prepared with cream, isinglass, and caramel.

ingredients.name: Drops of vanilla and bergamot oil
ingredients.sourceText: Drops of vanilla and bergamot oil

ingredients.name: Brown caramel sugar, dissolved cochineal, saffron decoction, spinach decoction for coloring
ingredients.sourceText: Brown caramel sugar, dissolved cochineal, saffron decoction, spinach decoction for coloring

steps: Beat 1 pot thick, sweet cream until very stiff foam.
Add 6 quarters isinglass, first dissolved in boiling water, a few drops of vanilla and bergamot oil, and sugar to taste—about 1 pound.

Color one part brown with brown caramel sugar, another red with dissolved cochineal, one yellow with saffron decoction, one green with spinach decoction, and thus you can vary the colors as desired in the different layers with which the jelly mold is filled; but each layer must be set before the next comes on.
Set the whole blancmange in a cold place to become stiff.
It can also be filled in small molds, but then given only one color.

title: Blanquet af Kalvekjod (Blanquette of Veal)
description: Prepared with veal, white pepper, and carrot.
steps: Cut {{source-0}} into small pieces and place in sufficient cold water to cover them; at the same time add half a teaspoon white pepper, a teaspoon salt, a good bunch of green herbs, half a scraped carrot, a peeled turnip and an onion in which 3 cloves are stuck
Bring to a gentle boil and skim carefully as long as scum appears, and cook until the meat is tender
Strain it, keeping the broth on the heat and wash the meat in cold water
Meanwhile make a white sauce by melting a little butter and stirring flour into it and then gradually adding 1½ pints of the broth
Add a little more pepper and salt if needed, and half a teaspoon grated nutmeg
When the sauce comes to a boil, whisk it with a whisk, add two small egg yolks, put the meat in and cook it a few minutes while stirring occasionally
It can be served with a tablespoon of chopped parsley sprinkled over it after it is poured onto a warm platter

title: Bleg-Selleri- og Østers-Salat (Celery and Oyster Salad)
description: A salad made with celery, oysters, and lemon juice.

ingredients.name: 1 can preserved oysters, containing approximately 375 grams (1/4 pound)
ingredients.sourceText: 1 can preserved oysters, containing approximately 375 grams (1/4 pound)

steps: Marinate the oysters in a mixture of oil, lemon juice, salt and a small amount of finely ground white pepper.
Set aside for a couple of hours in an icebox or cold place.
Rinse the celery and cut out the most tender and best of it in very thin slices.
Place them in a bowl and add a piece of ice.
When the salad is to be served, drain the celery together with the oysters.
Place a layer in the salad bowl, cover with mayonnaise, then again celery and oysters and mayonnaise as the top layer.
Garnish with watercress.
Make the mayonnaise from 2 egg yolks.

title: Blodpolser (Blood Sausages)
description: Prepared with pork or beef, barley, and pork.

ingredients.name: 3 spoonfuls dried, finely chopped thyme and marjoram leaves
ingredients.sourceText: 3 spoonfuls dried, finely chopped thyme and marjoram leaves

ingredients.name: pork lard, cut into small cubes
ingredients.sourceText: pork lard, cut into small cubes

steps: Clean the intestines completely inside and out by scraping, turning and filling them repeatedly in lukewarm water
When they are completely smooth and clear, place them in cold water with celery leaves and let them stand overnight
The same day the intestines are cleaned, pour boiling water over a suitable quantity of medium-fine barley grains (or half barley grains and half rye flour)
After stirring well, drain off almost all the water and let the grains stand until the next day
The next day, pour 1½ gallons of pork blood, still warm from slaughter, through a sieve over them, and let them stand again until the next day, stirring regularly

Add 3 spoonfuls of dried, finely chopped and sieved thyme and marjoram leaves to the blood, along with 1 spoonful crushed allspice, 3 spoonfuls crushed cloves, ¼ pound powdered sugar, a little salt and {{source-8}}
Stir the whole to a thick consistency
Drain the water from the intestines and lay them in lukewarm water
Blow down into them to see where there are holes, and cut them there
Tie one end, put the sausage horn in the other end, and through it fill the sausage with a spoon while stirring often
For each spoonful add a couple of cubes of pork lard
Fill the intestines only about half full, tie them off and press the sausage mixture around in them so that the raisins and meat cubes are well distributed
Place them in lukewarm water, and when 4 or 6 are filled, place them in a kettle with boiling water
Add the thyme stalks to the boiling water
During cooking prick them here and there
Cook for a good half hour or until a fine stick inserted in them no longer becomes colored from blood
Serve with powdered white sugar and powdered cinnamon or sieved cloves in melted butter

title: Blommer År. 1. (Pickled Plums No. 1)
description: Prepared with plums, vinegar, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: Half gill vinegar per pound of plums
ingredients.sourceText: Half gill vinegar per pound of plums

ingredients.name: Half pound powdered sugar per pound of plums
ingredients.sourceText: Half pound powdered sugar per pound of plums

ingredients.name: Fresh bay leaves (optional, for serving with roasted meat)
ingredients.sourceText: Fresh bay leaves (optional, for serving with roasted meat)

steps: Plums must be fully ripe. Dry them, prick them with a pointed wooden stick or needle and place them in a crock, where they are covered with half a gill of vinegar per pound of plums and left until the next day.

Pour off the vinegar and add half pound of powdered sugar per pound of plums. Heat this on the fire, and when it is just melted, add the plums and turn them a couple of times around so that those that were at the bottom come to the top.

When it begins to boil, pour it into the crock, leave uncovered until the next day, pour into another crock so that the syrup can reach all the plums, and the day after set the whole thing back on the fire, but stop as soon as it begins to boil.
Two days later set it on the fire again, and now cook the plums until they are not sour by the stones, usually in half an hour. Then place them in a strainer so the syrup can drain off.

Cook the syrup a good quarter hour, or until it is smooth, with whole cinnamon and cloves. Pour it into a crock, and when it is cold, place the plums in it, but not too many, so there can be sufficient syrup around the plums.
The next day tie them up. If there is more syrup than can be with the plums, pour this into bottles. If one wishes to use these plums with roast, it is good to add a few fresh bay leaves.

title: Blommer År. 2. (Pickled Plums No. 2)
description: Prepared with powdered sugar, vinegar, and water.

ingredients.name: powdered sugar per pound of plums
ingredients.sourceText: 3 pounds powdered sugar per pound of plums

ingredients.name: Half gill vinegar per pound of plums
ingredients.sourceText: Half gill vinegar per pound of plums

ingredients.name: water per pound of plums
ingredients.sourceText: 1 tablespoon water per pound of plums

steps: For each pound of plums, take 3 pounds powdered sugar, which is put on the fire with half gill vinegar and 1 tablespoon water.
When it is melted, pour it over the plums, which have first been dried, pricked and placed in a crock.

After 3 to 4 days, during which the plums are poured each day into another crock so that the syrup can reach around them, set them over the fire where they are cooked until they are not sour by the stones, about three-quarters of an hour.
Then place them in a coarse strainer and from there in a crock which is filled half full with them.
Cook the syrup with cinnamon and cloves for a quarter hour or until it is smooth. Pour it warm over the plums, which are tied up the next day.
Plums can be preserved in the same way with half pound sugar and half gill vinegar per pound, but then less syrup is obtained.

title: Blødkogte Æg (Soft-Boiled Eggs)
description: Prepared with eggs and salt.
steps: Wash the eggs in salt water and place them in an egg net, which is lowered into the boiling water. When boiling eggs, account must be taken for the size of the eggs. Very large, fresh eggs easily tolerate boiling for 4 minutes; otherwise the common rule is 3 minutes. 6 to 7 minutes are needed for the white to be firm and the yolk soft for cut eggs. The eggs must not be boiled in too much water or under a cover, as it causes them to crack easily. Fresh eggs have a greater density than water and therefore sink to the bottom of the pot, whereas less good ones float on top. Soft-boiled eggs are arranged immediately either in an egg coddler or on a platter lined with a napkin, which is folded over the eggs and garnished with parsley.

title: Boeuf a la Mode (Beef Braised in Wine)
description: Prepared with beef, bacon, and broth.
steps: For this several beef rump steaks are used, and since these are usually lean, many lard them with bacon pieces, done by cutting a deep slit in several places in the meat, taking small bacon pieces, dipping them in pepper and ginger and pushing them as deep in as possible.
If the cut gapes, it is closed together with a small skewer or with one of the bacon strips with which the roast is larded on the outside.
Such bacon strips must be cut lengthwise through the meat; if taken crosswise, they break apart.

The roast is then dusted with flour, but not more than can be well rubbed in; then it is browned on all sides in butter, and one must not take more of it than exactly necessary, for then the roast would become less brown.
When all sides are brown, the roast is taken up, a good spoonful of flour is browned in the butter that is in the pan; this is filled out with about 3 quarts of hot broth little by little.
The roast is placed back in and some whole onions, a couple of anchovies, a small handful of bay leaves, some pieces of whole ginger and whole peppercorns are added to the sauce.
This all boils together under a lid until the roast is tender, then the sauce is strained, thinned if it is too thick, and whatever oysters or gravy you have is added.

title: Boiled Fish with Oyster Sauce (Kogt Fisk med Østers-Sauce)
description: A sauce made with cod, oysters, and egg yolk.
steps: Clean and boil 2 pounds of cod in salt water according to instructions.
Once the fish is done, remove the pot from heat and set aside.
In the meantime, place 1 pint of oysters over heat to cook in their own sauce.
Once cooked, strain the oysters and return the sauce to heat to bring it to a boil.
Melt 1 ounce of butter in a frying pan over heat, stir in 1 ounce of flour, and when it bubbles, stir in the boiling oyster sauce.
Even out the sauce with 1 well-beaten egg yolk, ½ teaspoon salt, and a little ground white pepper.
Add the oysters and serve the sauce in a sauce boat.

title: Boiled Smoked Ham with Madeira
description: Prepared with ham, madeira, and broth.

ingredients.name: One smoked, lightly salted ham, approximately 4 kg (8 lbs)
ingredients.sourceText: One smoked, lightly salted ham, approximately 4 kg (8 lbs)

steps: Blanch the smoked, lightly salted ham over heat in abundant boiling water, where it must boil very gently for 2½ hours, or until the rind easily comes off.
Transfer the ham to another pot that is no larger than strictly necessary, and cover with 1 bottle of Madeira.
Let it boil for ½ hour very gently under a very tightly fitting lid, so that all the wine does not evaporate.
At serving, cover it with a gentle, reduced, strong broth and serve hot with vegetables.
Make a sauce by baking butter and flour together, and thin it with a mixture of the reduced broth and the Madeira in which the ham was cooked.

title: Bordelaise-Sauce (Bordelaise Sauce)
description: A sauce made with shallots, red wine, and brown sauce.

ingredients.name: A couple of tablespoons finely chopped shallots
ingredients.sourceText: A couple of tablespoons finely chopped shallots

ingredients.name: ½ liter (½ pot) good brown sauce
ingredients.sourceText: ½ liter (½ pot) good brown sauce

ingredients.sourceText: 50 to 75 grams (10 to 15 ounces) small marrow dumplings

steps: A couple of tablespoons finely chopped shallots, among which there should preferably be a clove of garlic, are sautéed in butter and covered with a good ¼ liter red wine.
This boils until some of the wine has evaporated, then ½ liter good, brown sauce is added, made as usual but it must be strong.

title: Bouillon (Beef Broth)
description: A soup made with beef, carrots, and celery.

ingredients.name: Beef with bones (such as shank, brisket, leg, breast, etc.)
ingredients.sourceText: Beef with bones (such as shank, brisket, leg, breast, etc.)

steps: Rinse the beef and place it in a pot with cold water, allowing 1 pot of water per pound of beef. The water should stand slightly above the meat, and the pot should be nearly full with a tightly fitting lid.
Bring the broth to a gentle boil over low heat until it begins to foam. Add a little salt, which helps bring the foam to the surface more readily.
Keep the broth simmering under a closed lid with even heat, skimming frequently until all impurities are removed.
When clean, add several well-rinsed whole soup vegetables: carrots, parsley roots, and celery, as well as a bundle of herbs tied with twine.
Add peeled onions, a few whole peppercorns, a small piece of ginger, and a small piece of candy sugar.
Continue simmering the broth over even heat with gentle cooking until the vegetables are tender, then remove them. Continue cooking the meat until it is completely tender.
When the broth is finished cooking, strain it and let it rest quietly for a quarter hour, then skim off the fat.
Serve the bouillon with an egg yolk and toasted bread slices, or use it as a base for other soups and sauces.

description: A soup made with beef, veal, and water.
steps: Chop the beef shank and veal shank. If the hen is to be used whole later, do not chop it; otherwise chop it as well.
Place all the meat over heat with 8 pots water and cook in the same manner as Bouillon No. 1.
When the soup is strained, pour it back into the pot without the sediment, and now cook it over gentle heat with regular stirring until it becomes brown and even, approximately like syrup.
It is then ready and poured onto a flat dish to cool and can be kept for a long time.
When you wish to use it, cut off appropriate pieces, which are dissolved in boiling water.

title: Brombær- og Ribs-Gelé (Blackberry and Currant Jelly)
description: Prepared with currant, blackberries, and sugar.

ingredients.name: Red currant juice, equal weight to blackberry juice
ingredients.sourceText: Red currant juice, equal weight to blackberry juice

ingredients.name: sugar (or corresponding weight to combined juices)
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 kg sugar (or corresponding weight to combined juices)

steps: Since blackberries are quite sweet, the best jelly is obtained by mixing blackberry and currant juice, half of each.

Place the blackberries in a pot and set over heat until they begin to release their juices well; then lift the pot off and crush the berries with a spoon before pouring into a scalded and tightly wrung jelly cloth.
The next day, weigh the juice and mix with an equal weight of completely clear currant juice without sugar.
After the sugar has been weighed and cooked as mentioned in No. 93, pour the juice into it: cook and skim for 10 minutes.
Fill the jelly into cups, which are tied up when it is partially cold and has begun to set.
The pulp remaining in the cloth is pressed through a very coarse sieve and used for Russian marmalade.

title: Brun Sky (Brown Gravy)
description: A sauce made with beef, onions, and carrots.
steps: In a heavy-bottomed casserole, melt {{source-0}} and let it run around the bottom.
Add 1/2 pound finely chopped beef kidney.
Slice approximately 6 pounds of medium-cut beef and lay it on the bottom of the casserole.
Over this, place peeled onions and slices of cleaned carrots and celery.
On top of this, layer scraps of meat and bone and well-rinsed roasting bones that have been chopped.
Place the whole over gentle heat for one hour, or better yet in a fairly warm oven, and watch that it does not burn. If necessary, thin the mixture with a little bouillon.
Then place the whole briefly over stronger heat, and pour in enough water so that it just covers the mixture.
Add a little salt, a small soup bunch, and about 10 peppercorns, then cook covered under gentle heat for approximately 4 to 5 hours.
Remove the vegetables and soup bunch, and when the gravy is done, strain it and set it aside to cool.
The longer the gravy cooks, the firmer it becomes, and the longer it can be kept.

Sprinkle in the flour and work well with a spoon, as the dough is too soft to handle by hand

Butter the baking sheet and place the cakes not too close together

Store in tin boxes for an extended period. Note: candied citrus peel and almonds can be omitted from the dough and the cakes will still be good

title: Brunet Smør (Browned Butter)
description: Prepared with butter and margarine.
steps: A mixture of the best margarine and good butter can be browned together in a pan just before serving.
It is sufficiently brown as soon as it has stopped foaming; then, if desired, the sediment can be strained out before it is poured into the sauce bowl.
To browned butter can be added lemon juice or vinegar, if it suits the dish it is to be served with.
Naturally, it is preferable to use only butter for this, but margarine is excellent for mixing with it.

title: Brunkaal (Braised Brown Cabbage)
description: Prepared with cabbage, butter or lard, and liquid or broth or gravy or water.
steps: Slice the white cabbage and place it in a pot in which a good slice of butter or lard has been browned.
Add a spoonful of sugar and brown the cabbage with regular stirring so it does not burn.
To speed up browning, coloring may be added.
Once the cabbage has sufficient color, add a little liquid, which can be broth, gravy, or water.

Season with salt and more sugar if necessary.
Serve with boiled sausages, boiled and fried bacon.
A piece of lightly salted, striped bacon can be rinsed, placed in the browned cabbage, and cooked in it, to be eaten with the cabbage.

Knead well with the hands.
Roll out the dough to half a finger's thickness in a round or oval shape.
Fold up the dough around the edge into tongues; in every other tongue place almonds, in the other raisins with a small lump of remaining butter.
Melt the rest of the butter and brush the cake with it, then sprinkle a good layer of ground cinnamon and powdered sugar.
If desired, thin slices of citron peel can be placed here and there.
Let the cake rise for 1/2 hour before it goes in the oven.

steps: Cook the sugar with water and a little egg white. During cooking, skim it well, and to test if it is cooked enough, dip a spoon in water and then in the sugar. When you bite the sugar you get on the spoon, it must release from your teeth; as long as it sticks, it is not cooked enough. The sugar can either be poured hot onto a buttered sheet and when it is almost cold, cut into square pieces; or it can be molded in forms created from dry starch on a sheet. Different flavors are given by the addition of cognac, rum, lemon or orange juice, chocolate, peppermint water, vanilla, and similar.

steps: From a large French bread, cut off the crust, and cut the bread into thick slices, which are dipped in milk and left covered for a couple of hours, after which they are mashed with a spoon.
200 grams of margarine is melted, and the bread is baked in it until it is well combined.
When the batter is slightly cooled, it is stirred with 12 egg yolks and finally with the beaten egg whites.

A little salt and sugar are added to taste, and the pudding can be seasoned either with crushed almonds, finely cut citron peel, raisins, orange essence, grated lemon zest, or 3 crushed vanilla tablets.
Serve with fruit sauces, ginger sauce, or red wine sauce.

title: Brød-Pletter (Bread Pancake Cakes)
description: A cake made with powdered sugar, bitter almonds, and wheat flour.

ingredients.name: Some slices not too fresh French bread
ingredients.sourceText: Some slices not too fresh French bread

steps: Soak some slices of not too fresh French bread in milk.
After taking them up, press them apart with a spoon.
Add powdered sugar, a little powdered cinnamon, some crushed bitter almonds, and a couple of tablespoonfuls wheat flour.
Beat 4 eggs with a little sweet cream and add to the rest.
Finally stir in 0.5 pint melted butter.
Bake somewhat thick cakes from this.
Put butter on for each new pan full.
Serve with powdered sugar and powdered cinnamon.

title: Brød-Suppe (Bread Soup)
description: A soup made with rye, white wine, and juice.
steps: Slice the rye bread small and boil in 3 quarts of water until smooth
Rub through a sieve and set back on heat with lemon zest and cinnamon

If you do not have sliced bread to use, the bread can be grated, and then the soup does not need to be strained

steps: Soak old rye bread in water for a few hours and cook it.

Prepare with rhubarb juice, sherry and sugar or with jam.

Serve with cream foam.

title: Brødbudding (Bread Pudding)
description: A pudding made with bread, milk or water, and raisins.
steps: Grate half a pound French bread, cut into pieces and dip very lightly in sweet milk or cold water, then let it stand covered for an hour. Then mash it with a spoon and bake with a quarter pound butter until it releases from the spoon, then place it in a deep dish to cool somewhat. When this is done, but while it is still warm, stir in a quarter pound cleaned raisins with the kernels removed, a quarter pound ground sugar, a little salt, cardamom or lemon zest, and 10 egg yolks. Lastly stir in the egg whites, which have been beaten to a foam, also carefully. The stirring takes about half an hour. Then put the mixture in a mold that is buttered and sprinkled with grated bread. Set the mold in boiling water, and the pudding must boil for 2 hours. Serve with sweet fruit sauce.

title: Butterdejg (Puff Pastry)
description: A pastry dish made with cake, margarine, and vinegar.
steps: Place flour on a pastry board and blend half of the cold margarine with the flour until very finely crumbled, using a large knife to chop the flour and butter together to keep hands cool
Make a well in the center of the flour and pour in the vinegar and cold water
Work together with the knife until a tough dough forms
Gather the dough together with quick, light hands and roll out with a pastry pin into a large sheet
Distribute the remaining margarine in small lumps over the dough
Fold the dough first into 3 parts and then again into 3 parts in the opposite direction, as if folding a napkin
Wrap in a cloth and set in a cold place for 1 hour
Roll out and fold the puff pastry 4 to 5 times with a few minutes between each folding, ensuring this is done in a cool kitchen and using only minimal flour for the rolling pin and board
The dough is then ready for use in various baked goods
A larger portion of puff pastry can be made at once but must be stored in a cold place and well covered to prevent it from developing a dry crust
The pastry is typically baked the day it is to be served, but it can also be baked the day before and reheated in the oven before serving

title: Butterdejg til Postejer (Puff Pastry for Pies)
description: A pastry dish made with cognac, butter, and flour.
steps: Wash the butter well in several changes of cold water until it becomes smooth and free of salt, then lay it in cold water.
Place {{source-1}} on a pastry board and make a depression in the middle, into which put 1 pint good cognac (or water) together with a piece of the butter.
Work this together with a little cold water until it becomes a suitably thick dough; but it must be worked well together until eyes appear in it.
Roll out the dough to the thickness of a straw and take the rest of the butter out of the water and pat it in a dry cloth, place it in the middle of the dough.
Fold the dough into three and beat well with a rolling pin.
Thus roll out the dough 4 to 5 times after each time folding it 4 to 5 sections and set aside to cool for a couple of hours.
When the dough is to be baked, roll it out to the thickness of a two-crown coin.

title: Butterdejgs-Æblekager (Butter Dough Apple Cakes)
description: A cake made with margarine, vinegar, and apples.
steps: Make butter dough from flour, margarine, water, and vinegar
Roll out a very thin layer that covers the baking sheet completely
Peel the apples, divide into 4 pieces, and remove the cores
Rinse them and place in a saucepan with a little water and cook until partly tender, but not until they become mush
Sweeten and cool before spreading over the dough and sprinkling with cinnamon
Roll out the remaining dough into a similar sheet and cover the apples with it
Press the cake together along the edges, brush with egg, and sprinkle with sugar
Bake in a well-heated oven for approximately half an hour
When the sheet is taken from the oven, cut the cake into small, square cakes
Sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve lukewarm
Can be decorated with whipped cream
These cakes can be made with different fruits, first cooked with sugar, such as gooseberries, rhubarb, plums, and dried apricots

title: Canton af Faarekjod (Stuffed Mutton Shoulder)
description: Prepared with mutton, onions, and breadcrumbs.
steps: The shoulder should not be cracked at the butcher; wash it and lay it on the table with the inner side up.
Remove the shoulder blade and cook it to be completely clean.

With a sharp, thin-bladed knife, cut out the lower joint of the bone and half of the second, breaking off halfway between the first and second joint and being careful not to tear the meat or cut through the skin.
Shape the end of the bone so it resembles a duck's beak.
Stuff the shoulder with a forcemeat or filling made as follows: peel 6 onions, cut them into pieces and cook them in three different changes of water.
Soak 8 ounces of breadcrumbs in lukewarm water and wring out in a clean cloth.
When the onions are tender, about half an hour, chop them and mix together with the breadcrumbs, a piece of butter, 10 egg yolks and a little salt and pepper.
After filling the skin with this, sew it and tie it together so it resembles a duck.
Place it in the roasting pan on some pieces of vegetables and roast in a hot oven about 20 minutes per pound.
Meanwhile, prepare carrots and parsnips by cutting them into small balls, cook them tender in well-salted boiling water and place them in cold water to preserve their color.
When the canton is done, remove it to a warm platter and keep warm without covering while the sauce is made.
Make the sauce from browned butter with a little flour, strain the gravy from the roasting pan with the vegetables into the sauce, and finally stir in a spoonful of raw cream and a little sugar.
Warm the root vegetables in the sauce and arrange them around the meat.
The shoulder blade, which should be scraped after being cooked and have the broad end chopped so it resembles a feather, is placed behind the canton, which is then served.

title: Champignons (Preserved Mushrooms)
description: Prepared with mushrooms and salt.

ingredients.name: Salt (100 grams per 1/2 kilogram of mushrooms)

steps: Extract the small, closed mushrooms first in boiled water as clarified in Nr. 217, then drain them on a sieve.
After draining well, place them in jars; for a larger portion one can use a well-cleaned butter tub.
Arrange the mushrooms on blocks with caps facing up and sprinkle salt between the layers.
Spread a piece of linen over them, then cover with a perforated wooden bottom of appropriate size to fit the tub and place a stone or other press on top.
Leave in this manner in a cool place.
Soak the mushrooms a few hours before use, changing the water several times during this period.
Salted mushrooms can be preserved throughout the winter if kept covered with a press on top.
Some of the brine that forms can be used in Mushroom-Soya (see the Cookbook).

title: Chartreuse med Bajerske Pølser (Chartreuse with Bavarian Sausages)
description: Prepared with sausages, cabbage, and carrots.
steps: A Chartreuse can either be cooked in a pudding mold without a tap or placed in the oven in a mold with a solid bottom. If the latter, a piece of paper buttered with butter and with some small holes cut in it can be placed over it to allow steam to escape. The mold used must be well buttered with cold butter.
Yellow and white carrots, which are half-cooked, are cut into thin slices and cut into equal sizes. They are pressed firmly against the bottom and sides of the mold to form a pattern.

The cabbage, which can be savoy cabbage, pointed cabbage, or white cabbage, is cut into 4 parts and cooked nearly tender in water. The stalks are cut off, and the water is pressed well out of the cabbage, which is chopped very coarsely with salt and pepper.

The previously decorated mold is lined with a 3 centimeter (1 inch) thick layer of cabbage, and the sausages are placed in the middle. Over this cabbage is laid again, and finally the Chartreuse is poured over with 125 gr (1/4 pound) melted butter.
It is cooked or baked for about an hour, carefully turned out onto a serving dish and served with good, brown sauce.

title: Cherries with Vinegar
description: Prepared with cherries, vinegar, and powdered sugar.
steps: The sugar can be chosen between powdered sugar, icing sugar or Demerara sugar, the latter gives the best juice.
Place the sugar in the pot in layers with the pitted berries, and pour the vinegar over.
The pot should initially be placed over low heat, while stirring occasionally.
As soon as the cherries boil, skim them and remove them on a colander, but not before they begin to wrinkle; usually one counts 10 minutes of boiling.
Pour the cherries, from which the juice must have drained well, into a jar, and reduce the juice until it is fairly thick.
Pour it boiling over the cherries, which can then be sealed immediately with parchment paper.
If desired, some pieces of whole cinnamon and some cloves can be boiled with the juice.

title: Chokolade-Budding (Chocolate Pudding)
description: A pudding made with coffee, isinglass, and cream.

ingredients.name: cream, whipped to stiff foam
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 L cream, whipped to stiff foam

ingredients.name: wheat flour or powdered starch
ingredients.sourceText: 2 teaspoons wheat flour or powdered starch

Add vanilla essence to the sauce

title: Chokolade-Budding (Chocolate Pudding)
description: A pudding made with chocolate, cream, and powdered sugar.

ingredients.name: isinglass or nearly 2 Ounces gelatine
ingredients.sourceText: 6 Ounces isinglass or nearly 2 Ounces gelatine

steps: Put the cream on the heat with the grated chocolate, powdered sugar, and isinglass or gelatine
Let it boil for about 15 minutes
Pour it out and stir until it is cold, but still fluid enough to be poured into the oiled mold so that a layer forms all over it, about as thick as a finger
Continue to turn the mold until the mixture is so stiff that it no longer moves
Smooth out the last layer evenly with a knife so that a hollow space remains in the center
Let the mold stand in this way until the next day
Then whip 1 Pint cream to stiff peaks with 2 Ounces white sugar, vanilla, and finally 1 Ounce dissolved gelatine
Fill the pudding with this mixture
After a couple of hours it can be turned onto a plate, but it must first be loosened on the sides with a knife; if it still does not slip out, place a hot cloth around the mold for a moment
A mold that holds 2.5 Quarts is adequate for this portion, which serves 16 persons

ingredients.sourceText: 6 egg whites, whipped with powdered icing sugar

Place the mixture in a deep porcelain pan in a moderately warm oven.

Serve with cooked bread or small rusks, and allow 1 pint of milk per person.

When the chutney is ready, it should resemble a thin porridge
Pour it into jars and bind with parchment paper

title: Citron som Lemon (Preserved Lemons)
description: Prepared with lemons, white pepper, and wine.
steps: Dry the lemons well and make a cross-cut at one end down to the middle of the lemon
Widen the cross-cuts and fill each one with a spoonful of salt
Stand the lemons in a dish with the whole end down
After they have stood uncovered for 8 days, turn them and let them stand the same length of time on the other end
Place them in an enameled pot side by side
Pour the drained brine over them and add 2 pieces Spanish pepper, {{source-3}}, and a few pieces scraped ginger
Add 2 pots best wine vinegar to the pot and place over a good heat of coals
Boil the lemons for half an hour over even heat until they are tender
Place them in a jar and pour the hot brine over them; if the brine is not sufficient, boil some vinegar and pour it hot into the jar
Sew a small but fairly roomy bag of white, open linen large enough to fill the upper part of the jar
Put {{source-6}} and 3-4 shallots in the bag
Boil this slightly while the lemons are cooking and place it over them in the jar
The next day, bind the jar in the usual way
After 3 months have passed, you can begin to use them; they become better by standing even longer

title: Citron- eller Appelsinskaller (Lemon or Orange Peel)
description: Prepared with lemon or orange peel, lemon juice, and sugar.

ingredients.name: (1 lb) lemon or orange peel
ingredients.sourceText: 1/2 kg (1 lb) lemon or orange peel

steps: Remove the peel from the fruit in 2 or 4 pieces and soak them in cold water for 5 days, changing the water daily.
After this time, place them over heat in cold water and cook them gently under a lid, usually for almost 1/2 hour.
Remove the peels and cut away all the white part before weighing.
Boil the sugar into a thin syrup with 1/2 l (1/2 pot) water, which is only poured over the peels once it has cooled, and let them sit covered for 2 to 3 days.
Pour the syrup into a pot and boil it until smooth together with the juice of 1 lemon.
Finally, give the peels one boil in it before placing them in the jars.
Reduce the syrup again until it is completely smooth, pour it boiling over the peels, and seal the jars immediately.

title: Citronol (Lemon Ale)
description: Prepared with lemons, yeast, and sugar.
steps: Pour the sugar together with 37 quarts of water into a clean kettle, boil for 1 hour, skim well, cool. When lukewarm, add the yeast. Cover the vessel with a lid, not a cloth, which would cause off-flavor. Let stand 2 or more days for fermentation. Carefully skim off the yeast foam, pour the ale into barrels. Slice the lemons without peeling and add them. Bung the barrel and place in the cellar. After 14 days the ale is ready for bottling. Pour 23 quarts of fresh spring water into the barrel and bottle it.

title: Clam Chowder (New Bedford Style)
description: Prepared with clams, pork, and onions.
steps: Rinse the clams thoroughly and place in a pot with 3 pints water.
When the shells open, remove the clams and chop them finely, reserving all the clam water.
Fry the pork slowly, remove the pieces, and fry or toast the onions.
Keep the chowder pot very clean to avoid scorching.
Add the onions with 1 quart hot water.
Pour in the clams, clam water, and pork pieces.
When boiling, add the potatoes.
When the potatoes are cooked, the dish is done.
Add a little crushed crackers and sweet milk before serving.

title: Consommé Royal (Royal Consommé)
description: A soup made with stock, sweetbreads, and butter or margarine.
steps: Blanch the sweetbreads and cook them tender in the economical stock
Cut half of the sweetbreads into very small dice and place in the tureen
Finely chop the remaining sweetbreads and sauté in a very little butter or vegetable margarine
Brown {{source-4}} and dilute with the stock, thickened with 6 egg yolks
Add a little paprika and Madeira to taste
Press the soup through a coarse sieve into the tureen
Serve with salt sticks
